title: Custom events
learningObjectives: Explain custom events and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: CustomEvent creates application-defined events that can carry detail data. dispatchEvent() sends the event to a target and invokes matching listeners synchronously through the DOM event system. Custom events can bubble and be cancelable when configured.
understand.whyItMatters: Custom events decouple modules by allowing one part of an application to announce something without importing every listener directly. Event names and detail shapes should be documented and versioned where needed.
understand.analogy: A custom event is a notice posted on a shared board; interested parts of the application can listen for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The listener receives the custom event and reads its structured detail payload. dispatchEvent invokes listeners synchronously.

examples.explanation: The listener receives the custom event and reads its structured detail payload. dispatchEvent invokes listeners synchronously.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Create a custom event for a bookmark change. Document the event name and detail schema, then listen from a separate component.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: Where is custom event payload data commonly stored?
questions.explanation: CustomEvent exposes its supplied payload through event.detail.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
